**24 things** run without being asked: 4 on a schedule, 16 for as long as the app is open, 3 waiting on something to happen, and 1 you arm yourself. 9 of them can call a model you pay for; the rest cost nothing to run. What each one is for is fixed by the app; when it fires, and whether it fires at all, is yours.

> These are the **shipped defaults**. Every value here lives in a config
> file you own once TESSERACT is installed, so your copy may differ — and
> should, once you tune it.


## On a schedule

Each of these is a row in the schedule you own, so the cadence beside it is the shipped default and yours to change.

| Name | Fires | What it does | What you would lose without it | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `capture` | every 5 minutes | Seals what the last few minutes produced into memory leaves, and recaps any conversation that has gone quiet. | Turns and terminal work would wait for the nightly pass, anything the machine lost before it would never be captured at all, and a conversation held anywhere would leave nothing behind — so the next one would start from nothing. | free · your library |
| `consolidate` | 23:00 every day | Settles the day into the library — digest, distil, lint, scrub, re-index, decay — and sweeps the agenda and the providers on the way. | The library would grow by accretion: duplicates never merged, broken links never repaired, indexes drifting from the files they describe. | paid · `chain_2` and whichever chain the work names · your library |
| `janitor_sweep` | every 24 hours | Reaps orphaned processes, scratch directories and dead controller sessions. | Killed runs leave behind processes holding ports and directories holding locks, and both outlive the thing that made them. | free · the machine |
| `watchman` | every hour, at 15 past | Reads what the runtime actually did and reports what broke. | Errors, restarts and stalled work would sit in log files nobody opens until something visible failed. | paid · `chain_1` · the machine |

## For as long as the app is running

These have no clock. They wake on an event, a message or a short interval of their own, and they stop when the app does.

| Name | What it does | What you would lose without it | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activity_subscriber` | Keeps one connection to the agent controller and mirrors its activity here. | Work running in the controller's own process would be invisible to every surface in the app. | free · reaching you |
| `alarm_tick` | Checks the alarm registry every ten seconds and fires what is due. | An alarm you set would arrive up to a minute late, which for the one thing you asked to be reminded of is the whole value of it. | free · reaching you |
| `autonomy_kernel` | Drains the event bus, scores what it finds, dispatches workers, and calls out one whose heartbeat has gone quiet. | Nothing the assistant decides to do for itself would ever be picked up, recovery after a crash would wait for a person, and a worker that died mid-task would stay listed as running. | paid · whichever chain the work names · your library |
| `brief_delivery` | Puts the morning brief in front of you at the hour you set. | The brief would be written every night and sit in a folder until you thought to go and look for it. | free · reaching you |
| `config_watcher` | Watches the config directory and re-applies a file the moment it is saved. | Every settings change would need a restart, and a restart mid-work is how a setting stops being changed at all. | free · the machine |
| `controller_heartbeat` | Touches the agent controller's heartbeat file while the daemon lives. | Nothing could tell a controller that died from one that is merely idle, so a dead one would keep its lanes and never be replaced. | free · the machine |
| `entity_signals_pump` | Pushes entity signals to an open session on a fixed interval. | The panels that watch live state would only update when you acted. | free · reaching you |
| `governor_detector` | Watches the kernel's own behaviour and pauses a source that misbehaves. | A loop that produced the same work repeatedly would keep producing it, and the first sign would be the bill. | free · the machine |
| `loop_lag_monitor` | Samples the event loop and reports what blocked it when it stalls. | A blocked loop stops health checks, heartbeats and inbound turns at once, and without this the only symptom is an app that feels slow. | free · the machine |
| `mcp_client_supervisor` | Keeps each configured outbound MCP server connected, reconnecting with backoff. | A server that dropped once would stay gone until the next restart, and its tools would simply be missing. | free · the machine |
| `mcp_session_sweep` | Closes MCP sessions whose client vanished without saying so. | Every abandoned session would hold its stream and its state open until the backend restarted. | free · the machine |
| `observer_subscriber` | Watches the turns of an attached session and proposes what to remember. | What is worth keeping would be decided only in the moment, by an assistant busy answering, and most of it would be lost. | paid · `chain_1` · your library |
| `pty_feed` | Drains a terminal pane's output and, while observing, offers its lines to the observer. | Terminal work would reach neither the screen nor the assistant, and what you do in a shell is half of what there is to learn. | paid · `chain_1` · your library |
| `scheduler_tick` | Wakes once a minute and fires whichever rows are due. | Nothing on a schedule would ever run — every row above depends on it. | free · the machine |
| `session_autosave` | Writes an open session to disk on your autosave interval. | A crash or a power cut would take every turn since the session opened, and those turns are what the library is built from. | free · your library |
| `telegram_poll` | Holds a long poll open to Telegram and hands each message to the session. | Messages sent to the assistant from a phone would arrive only when something else happened to ask. | free · reaching you |

## When something happens

Waiting on a named event rather than on a time.

| Name | Fires | What it does | What you would lose without it | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `provider_probe` | when real traffic has failed over from a provider's primary | Checks every model you have configured, once real traffic has already fallen back from one of them. | A key that expired at breakfast would go unnoticed until the nightly check, and every role would spend the day quietly running on its second choice. | paid · whichever chain the work names · the machine |
| `skill_refinement` | when enough new skill uses have been logged to judge one | Reads how your skills have been performing and offers a rewrite of one that keeps ending in errors or corrections. | A skill that quietly misleads the assistant goes on misleading it. Without this, the usage log records that and nobody reads it. | paid · `chain_2` · your library |
| `skill_suggest` | when enough new daily digests have accumulated to read across | Reads across recent days of work and points out a task you keep repeating that no skill covers yet. | The library only grows when somebody notices a repeated shape. It never drafts a skill — it says what it saw, and you decide. | paid · `chain_2` · your library |

## When you ask for it

Nothing here runs until you arm it.

| Name | What it does | What you would lose without it | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scheduled_task` | Runs a recurring task you described, on the cadence you gave it. | Asking for something to happen every week would mean writing a job module for it, which puts it out of reach from a conversation. | paid · `chain_2` · reaching you |

## What the cost column means

**Free** work runs on this machine and calls nothing you are billed for. **Free · local model** needs a local model server running and still costs nothing to use. **Paid** means a call to a provider you hold a key for, on the chain named beside it — and where the chain is chosen by the work rather than fixed in advance, it says so.

Nothing here is billed per run in advance. What each of these actually spends is capped, and the ceilings are on the [Costs](/reference/costs/) page.

## Why every entry has to say what it is for

An entry that cannot say what would be lost without it is one nobody decided to keep — it was inherited. The runtime refuses to start with a blank in either column, which is why this page can be generated at all rather than written from memory.
